Hi Grace — thanks for the clear questions. Below is a concise, technical statement you can include in procurement; let us know if you want this redlined into contract language. I’ll also attach the SOC2 excerpt and the HIPAA Q&A template (see attachments).

Definitive statement (hosted API defaults and options):

- Default hosted behavior (no customer opt-in):
  * Prompts and model-generated outputs are processed in-memory and are not persisted to long-term storage for the purposes of product analytics by default. Transient debugging traces and request metadata are stored for 7 days to support incident triage.
  * Audit trails (request id, timestamp, model/version, latency, route decision) are retained for 365 days for security and abuse detection; these traces do not contain full model outputs unless the customer explicitly enables "debug logging".

- Optional hosted contract add-ons (by request / contractual amendment):
  * Extended retention window for traces and persisted artifacts (30 / 90 / custom days) can be offered with a contractual commitment and associated fee.
  * EU-only regional tenancy is available on the hosted plan for customers who require residency; data is pinned to EU regions (Google Cloud EU regions) and processing follows GDPR controls in our DPA.

- Dedicated & Private deployments:
  * For Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private (VPC/on-prem), customers control retention policies and keys. By default, Redwood does not access model inputs/outputs unless the customer enables telemetry sharing for support. For Private on-prem, data never traverses Redwood-managed control plane if configured accordingly.

- PII handling and redaction:
  * We offer an optional PII-scrubbing pipeline that can run client-side (recommended) or in our hosted preprocessing step. When enabled, the pipeline detects high-risk fields (SSNs, credit card numbers, MRNs) and either masks or hashes values before any logging occurs.
  * KV cache used by the runtime is kept in-memory; it is encrypted in transit and not written to disk in hosted mode. Instances flush in-memory cache on restart; Dedicated deployments may optionally enable encrypted checkpoints but only with explicit customer consent.

- Deletion & data subject requests:
  * Customers can request deletion of retained traces and persisted artifacts via support; standard SLA for deletion is 5 business days for hosted artifacts, and configurable for Dedicated/Private deployments as part of the SOW.

- Evidence & artifacts:
  * SOC2 Type II report excerpt, data flow diagrams, and a HIPAA mapping template are available; I’ve attached the HIPAA Q&A template we typically provide to health customers.

Next steps:
- If Aurelia needs 90-day retention for audit traces and EU residency, we recommend either a Hosted-EU contract add-on (we will ship a residency guarantee + 90-day retention clause) or Dedicated capacity if you want strict isolation and customer-controlled keys. We can produce a short SOW amendment for either path.

I’ll follow up separately with a suggested contract clause and a draft DocuSign link for the 90-day option if you want to proceed.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
